**Jonathan Gershuny** is Professor of Economic Sociology in the Social Research Institute, University College London, and Emeritus Professor of Sociology, University of Oxford. He is the Director of the ESRC Centre for Time Use Research (2014-2024), also funded by an Advanced Grant from the European Research Council and by the US National Institutes of Health. He was previously a Statutory Professor of Sociology and Head of Oxford University’s Sociology Department. Appointed CBE 2017, he gave the first Millennium Lecture at 10 Downing Street in 1999 and won the Silver Medal of the Market Research Society in 1986.

Both  scholars  and  the  popular  press  have  expressed  concern  regarding  the  potential  prevalence  of

date  has  been  inconclusive  as  to  whether  such  individuals  are  more  likely  to  emerge  as  leaders  or  
whether  they  are  (in)effective  leaders.  To  clarify  the  state  of  the  literature,  we  conducted  a  
meta-analysis  on  the  association  between  psychopathic  personality  characteristics  and  leadership  
emergence,  leadership  effectiveness,  and  transformational  leadership.  Our  results,  based  on  data  
from  92  independent  samples,  showed  a  weak  positive  correlation  for  psychopathic  tendencies  and  
leadership  emergence,  a  weak  negative  association  for  psychopathic  tendencies  and  leadership  
effectiveness,  and  a  moderate  negative  correlation  for  psychopathic  tendencies  and  transformational  
leadership.  Subgroup  analyses  on  methodological  factors  did  not  indicate  any  differences  from  the  
main  results.  However,  moderator  analyses  showed  a  gender  difference  in  these  associations  such  
that  psychopathic  tendencies  in  men  were  weakly  positively  correlated  with  leadership  emergence  
and  effectiveness  and  negatively  correlated  with  transformational  leadership,  while  psychopathic  
tendencies  in  women  were  negatively  associated  with  effectiveness  and  transformational  leadership,  
and  largely  unassociated  with  emergence.  In  addition,  small  but  consistent  curvilinear  associations  
were  found  for  all  leadership  criteria.  Overall,  these  results  suggest  that  concern  over  psychopathic

whether  they  are  (in)effective  leaders.  To  clarify  the  state  of  the  literature,  we  conducted  a  
meta-analysis  on  the  association  between  psychopathic  personality  characteristics  and  leadership  
emergence,  leadership  effectiveness,  and  transformational  leadership.  Our  results,  based  on  data  
from  92  independent  samples,  showed  a  weak  positive  correlation  for  psychopathic  tendencies  and

effectiveness,  and  a  moderate  negative  correlation  for  psychopathic  tendencies  and  transformational  
leadership.  Subgroup  analyses  on  methodological  factors  did  not  indicate  any  differences  from  the  
main  results.  However,  moderator  analyses  showed  a  gender  difference  in  these  associations  such

The **Iași National Theatre** (or **Vasile Alecsandri National Theater**; in [Romanian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanian_language "Romanian language"): Teatrul Național Vasile Alecsandri) in [Iași](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i "Iași"), [Romania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romania "Romania"), is the oldest national theatre and one of the most prestigious theatrical institutions in Romania. In 1956, it was given the name of the renowned Romanian playwright and poet [Vasile Alecsandri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vasile_Alecsandri "Vasile Alecsandri"). The building also hosts the [Iași Romanian National Opera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i_Romanian_National_Opera "Iași Romanian National Opera").
[![Image 3](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4e/TNI_1846.jpg/250px-TNI_1846.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:TNI_1846.jpg)
The old building of the National Theatre, 1846

The first dramatic play presented in the Romanian language (and one of the first theatrical performance in Romanian[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i_National_Theatre#cite_note-3)) was _Mirtil and Hloe_,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i_National_Theatre#cite_note-Gessner1850-4) adapted and staged by [Gheorghe Asachi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gheorghe_Asachi "Gheorghe Asachi"), and held in the capital (Jassy/Iași) of [Moldavia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moldavia "Moldavia"), on 27 December 1816.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i_National_Theatre#cite_note-5) In 1834, a Romanian production took place in Iași on the stage of the [Théâtre de varieté](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Th%C3%A9%C3%A2tre_des_Vari%C3%A9t%C3%A9s_(Ia%C8%99i) "Théâtre des Variétés (Iași)"), built in 1832 for the French Fouraux troupe.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The National Theatre was founded on 15 May 1840, as the _Great Theatre of Moldavia_, when the Romanian language troupe, led by [Costache Caragiali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Costache_Caragiale "Costache Caragiale"), was united with the French troupe, under a single direction of [Vasile Alecsandri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vasile_Alecsandri "Vasile Alecsandri") and the management of Costache Caragiali.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i_National_Theatre#cite_note-6) On 22 December 1846, a new audience hall was inaugurated in the former mansion of [Prince](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_rulers_of_Moldavia "List of rulers of Moldavia")[Mihail Sturdza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mihail_Sturdza "Mihail Sturdza"), on the [Hill of Copou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seven_hills_of_Ia%C8%99i "Seven hills of Iași").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i_National_Theatre#cite_note-7)

On the night of 17/18 February 1888, the theatre building was destroyed by the fire. Efforts to build the new theatre edifice culminated in 1894 when a contract was signed with the Viennese architects [Ferdinand Fellner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Fellner "Ferdinand Fellner") and [Hermann Helmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermann_Helmer "Hermann Helmer"), who designed several theatres and palaces across Europe, including the theatres in [Cluj-Napoca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cluj-Napoca_National_Theatre "Cluj-Napoca National Theatre"), [Oradea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oradea "Oradea"), [Timișoara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timi%C8%99oara "Timișoara") and [Chernivtsi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chernivtsi "Chernivtsi") (Romanian: Cernăuți).
[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ca/Teatrul_Na%C5%A3ional_Interior.jpg/250px-Teatrul_Na%C5%A3ional_Interior.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Teatrul_Na%C5%A3ional_Interior.jpg)
The main auditorium

For the building work, a contract was signed with a Bucharest company, and the power station was built by a company from Berlin. The Theatre’s power station also supplied with electricity the 12 electric-arc lamps lighting the Theatre Square, marking the beginning of electrification in the city of Iași. The works to building took two years, and on 1 and 2 December 1896, the inauguration festivities took place with [Flechtenmacher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Flechtenmacher?action=edit&redlink=1 "Alexander Flechtenmacher (page does not exist)")'s _National Overture_, the vaudevilles _Muza de la Burdujeni_ (_The Muse from Burdujeni_) by [Costache Negruzzi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Costache_Negruzzi "Costache Negruzzi") and _Cinel-cinel_ (_The Riddle_) by Vasile Alecsandri, as well as the verse comedy _Poetul romantic_ (_The Romantic Poet_) by [Matei Millo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matei_Millo "Matei Millo").
The Iași National Theatre building is listed in the [National Register of Historic Monuments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Register_of_Historic_Monuments_in_Romania "National Register of Historic Monuments in Romania").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i_National_Theatre#cite_note-8)
With a [Neoclassic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neoclassic_style "Neoclassic style") exterior and a richly decorated interior in [Rococo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rococo "Rococo") and [Baroque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baroque "Baroque") styles, the building is considered one of the most elegant in Romania.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i_National_Theatre#cite_note-9)

The main auditorium is organised in stalls, boxes and a balcony. The curtain painted by the Viennese M. Lenz, presents in the middle, an allegory of life with its three stages and, to the right side, the allegory of [Romanian Unification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Romania "Greater Romania"). The left-hand side, painted by Lenz’s apprentice, differs from the rest of the curtain in style and colouring.
The ceiling and the iron curtain were painted by Alexander Goltz. The iron curtain, which completely separates the scene from the hall, shows ornaments placed symmetrically, while the ceiling has as a narrative basis the Archetypal Story, shown in paradisiacal allegories, with nymphs and cupids framed in rococo stucco.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i_National_Theatre#cite_note-10)
The 1,418 electric lights and the chandelier with 109 Venetian crystal lamps light up the playhouse.

Efforts to build the new theatre edifice culminated in 1894 when a contract was signed with the Viennese architects [Ferdinand Fellner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Fellner "Ferdinand Fellner") and [Hermann Helmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermann_Helmer "Hermann Helmer"), who designed several theatres and palaces across Europe, including the theatres in [Cluj-Napoca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cluj-Napoca_National_Theatre "Cluj-Napoca National Theatre"), [Oradea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oradea "Oradea"), [Timișoara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timi%C8%99oara "Timișoara") and [Chernivtsi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chernivtsi "Chernivtsi") (Romanian: Cernăuți).
[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ca/Teatrul_Na%C5%A3ional_Interior.jpg/250px-Teatrul_Na%C5%A3ional_Interior.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Teatrul_Na%C5%A3ional_Interior.jpg)
The main auditorium

For the building work, a contract was signed with a Bucharest company, and the power station was built by a company from Berlin. The works to building took two years, and on 1 and 2 December 1896, the inauguration festivities took place with [Flechtenmacher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Flechtenmacher?action=edit&redlink=1 "Alexander Flechtenmacher (page does not exist)")'s _National Overture_, the vaudevilles _Muza de la Burdujeni_ (_The Muse from Burdujeni_) by [Costache Negruzzi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Costache_Negruzzi "Costache Negruzzi") and _Cinel-cinel_ (_The Riddle_) by Vasile Alecsandri, as well as the verse comedy _Poetul romantic_ (_The Romantic Poet_) by [Matei Millo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matei_Millo "Matei Millo").
The Iași National Theatre building is listed in the [National Register of Historic Monuments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Register_of_Historic_Monuments_in_Romania "National Register of Historic Monuments in Romania").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C5%9Fi_National_Theatre#cite_note-8)
With a [Neoclassic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neoclassic_style "Neoclassic style") exterior and a richly decorated interior in [Rococo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rococo "Rococo") and [Baroque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baroque "Baroque") styles, the building is considered one of the most elegant in Romania.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C5%9Fi_National_Theatre#cite_note-9)

Lenz, presents in the middle, an allegory of life with its three stages and, to the right side, the allegory of [Romanian Unification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Romania "Greater Romania"). The **Iași National Theatre** (or **Vasile Alecsandri National Theater**; in [Romanian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanian_language "Romanian language"): Teatrul Național Vasile Alecsandri) in [Iași](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i "Iași"), [Romania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romania "Romania"), is the oldest national theatre and one of the most prestigious theatrical institutions in Romania. In 1956, it was given the name of the renowned Romanian playwright and poet [Vasile Alecsandri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vasile_Alecsandri "Vasile Alecsandri"). The building also hosts the [Iași Romanian National Opera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i_Romanian_National_Opera "Iași Romanian National Opera").
[![Image 3](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4e/TNI_1846.jpg/250px-TNI_1846.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:TNI_1846.jpg)
The old building of the National Theatre, 1846
texts.2: The first dramatic play presented in the Romanian language (and one of the first theatrical performance in Romanian[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C5%9Fi_National_Theatre#cite_note-3)) was _Mirtil and Hloe_,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C5%9Fi_National_Theatre#cite_note-Gessner1850-4) adapted and staged by [Gheorghe Asachi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gheorghe_Asachi "Gheorghe Asachi"), and held in the capital (Jassy/Iași) of [Moldavia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moldavia "Moldavia"), on 27 December 1816.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C5%9Fi_National_Theatre#cite_note-5) In 1834, a Romanian production took place in Iași on the stage of the [Théâtre de varieté](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Th%C3%A9%C3%A2tre_des_Vari%C3%A9t%C3%A9s_(Ia%C8%99i) "Théâtre des Variétés (Iași)"), built in 1832 for the French Fouraux troupe.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
texts.3: The National Theatre was founded on 15 May 1840, as the _Great Theatre of Moldavia_, when the Romanian language troupe, led by [Costache Caragiali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Costache_Caragiale "Costache Caragiale"), was united with the French troupe, under a single direction of [Vasile Alecsandri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vasile_Alecsandri "Vasile Alecsandri") and the management of Costache Caragiali.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C5%9Fi_National_Theatre#cite_note-6) On 22 December 1846, a new audience hall was inaugurated in the former mansion of [Prince](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_rulers_of_Moldavia "List of rulers of Moldavia")[Mihail Sturdza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mihail_Sturdza "Mihail Sturdza"), on the [Hill of Copou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seven_hills_of_Ia%C8%99i "Seven hills of Iași").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C5%9Fi_National_Theatre#cite_note-7)
texts.4:
On the night of 17/18 February 1888, the theatre building was destroyed by the fire. Efforts to build the new theatre edifice culminated in 1894 when a contract was signed with the Viennese architects [Ferdinand Fellner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Fellner "Ferdinand Fellner") and [Hermann Helmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermann_Helmer "Hermann Helmer"), who designed several theatres and palaces across Europe, including the theatres in [Cluj-Napoca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cluj-Napoca_National_Theatre "Cluj-Napoca National Theatre"), [Oradea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oradea "Oradea"), [Timișoara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timi%C8%99oara "Timișoara") and [Chernivtsi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chernivtsi "Chernivtsi") (Romanian: Cernăuți).
[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ca/Teatrul_Na%C5%A3ional_Interior.jpg/250px-Teatrul_Na%C5%A3ional_Interior.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Teatrul_Na%C5%A3ional_Interior.jpg)
The main auditorium
texts.5:
For the building work, a contract was signed with a Bucharest company, and the power station was built by a company from Berlin. The Theatre’s power station also supplied with electricity the 12 electric-arc lamps lighting the Theatre Square, marking the beginning of electrification in the city of Iași. The works to building took two years, and on 1 and 2 December 1896, the inauguration festivities took place with [Flechtenmacher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Flechtenmacher?action=edit&redlink=1 "Alexander Flechtenmacher (page does not exist)")'s _National Overture_, the vaudevilles _Muza de la Burdujeni_ (_The Muse from Burdujeni_) by [Costache Negruzzi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Costache_Negruzzi "Costache Negruzzi") and _Cinel-cinel_ (_The Riddle_) by Vasile Alecsandri, as well as the verse comedy _Poetul romantic_ (_The Romantic Poet_) by [Matei Millo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matei_Millo "Matei Millo").
The Iași National Theatre building is listed in the [National Register of Historic Monuments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Register_of_Historic_Monuments_in_Romania "National Register of Historic Monuments in Romania").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C5%9Fi_National_Theatre#cite_note-8)
With a [Neoclassic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neoclassic_style "Neoclassic style") exterior and a richly decorated interior in [Rococo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rococo "Rococo") and [Baroque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baroque "Baroque") styles, the building is considered one of the most elegant in Romania.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C5%9Fi_National_Theatre#cite_note-9)
texts.6:
The main auditorium is organised in stalls, boxes and a balcony. The curtain painted by the Viennese M. Lenz, presents in the middle, an allegory of life with its three stages and, to the right side, the allegory of [Romanian Unification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Romania "Greater Romania"). The left-hand side, painted by Lenz’s apprentice, differs from the rest of the curtain in style and colouring.
The ceiling and the iron curtain were painted by Alexander Goltz. The iron curtain, which completely separates the scene from the hall, shows ornaments placed symmetrically, while the ceiling has as a narrative basis the Archetypal Story, shown in paradisiacal allegories, with nymphs and cupids framed in rococo stucco.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C5%9Fi_National_Theatre#cite_note-10)
The 1,418 electric lights and the chandelier with 109 Venetian crystal lamps light up the playhouse.
